overview: Nan Madol was a ceremonial centre associated with the Saudeleur on Pohnpei. Its architecture provides evidence for monumental engineering and concentrated chiefly authority; continuing Pohnpeian institutions must be distinguished from the earlier dynasty.

items.text: Builders assembled artificial islets with basalt and coral. Large columnar stones were brought from other parts of Pohnpei and laid in alternating architectural patterns.
Stone residences, temples and mortuary structures share a landscape of waterways. UNESCO dates the principal described remains to 1200 to 1500 CE.
Elite residences and the arrangement of the city separated chiefly occupants from the broader population. Buildings express differences in social status.
Altars, temples and priestly activity made the centre a spiritual as well as political place. Oral traditions require attribution when describing individual rulers.
The archaeological landscape remains connected to Pohnpei's ceremonial traditions and the Nahnmwarki system. Residential abandonment did not erase its significance.
